elements.name: Trigger (Stream Processing)
elements.aka: triggers, watermark trigger, processing-time trigger, repeated/composite triggers, early/on-time/late firings (panes), accumulation mode (discarding/accumulating/retracting, companion policy)
elements.what: A declarative mechanism that decides WHEN the accumulated contents of a window are materialized and emitted, driven by signals such as watermark passage, processing time, element count, or composites of these.
elements.problem: Windowing says where in event time data is grouped and the watermark says when input is believed complete, but neither says when to emit results; a trigger decouples output timing from input completeness, enabling early speculative results and late corrections instead of a single emit-at-watermark policy.
elements.named_in: The Dataflow Model (Akidau et al., PVLDB 8(12), 2015, sec. 2.3); modern canonical treatment: Streaming Systems (Akidau, Chernyak, Lax, 2018) and the Apache Beam programming guide (sec. 9 'Triggers', verified live 2026-07-10)
elements.tags: streaming; databases; distributed-adjacent but implementable inside a single stream operator/engine component; complements stream-windowing and event-time-watermark (distinct mechanism: output timing, not grouping or completeness)

elements.name: Semantic Model
elements.what: The in-memory model that a DSL parse populates and that the rest of the system executes against, kept deliberately separate from the parser and from any syntax tree.
elements.problem: Binding behavior directly to parsing (or to the syntax tree) entangles language processing with domain logic; a separate semantic model lets the same model be populated by multiple syntaxes, tested without parsing, and evolved independently of the grammar.
elements.named_in: Fowler, Domain-Specific Languages (Addison-Wesley, 2010), ch. 11; martinfowler.com/dslCatalog ('The model that's populated by a DSL', verified live 2026-07-10)
elements.tags: DSL processing; pairs with abstract-syntax-tree (the syntax-side representation) and embedded-domain-specific-language

elements.name: Expression Builder
elements.what: An object, or family of objects, that provides a fluent interface layered over a normal command-query API, translating chained expression-style calls into calls on the underlying objects.
elements.problem: Putting fluent methods directly on domain objects pollutes their command-query API and couples them to one DSL syntax; a separate builder layer isolates the fluent facade so the domain API stays conventional and multiple fluent syntaxes can coexist.
elements.named_in: Fowler, Domain-Specific Languages (Addison-Wesley, 2010), ch. 32; martinfowler.com/dslCatalog ('An object, or family of objects, that provides a fluent interface over a normal command-query API', verified live 2026-07-10)
elements.tags: internal DSLs; distinct from fluent-interface (the style) — this is the dedicated builder object that carries the style; composes with builder and method chaining

parked_architecture.name: Distributed Snapshot / Checkpoint Barrier (Chandy-Lamport; Flink Asynchronous Barrier Snapshotting)
parked_architecture.named_in: Chandy & Lamport, 'Distributed Snapshots: Determining Global States of Distributed Systems' (ACM TOCS 3(1), 1985); Carbone et al., 'Lightweight Asynchronous Snapshots for Distributed Dataflows' (2015, Flink ABS)
parked_architecture.rationale: Fails altitude upward: a protocol for capturing a consistent global state across the processes and channels of a distributed dataflow — barrier markers flow between workers over network channels. It is a system-level coordination protocol, not a mechanism implementable inside one program or component; the in-engine feel of Flink's barriers does not change that the mechanism's subject is inter-process global state. Phase 3 candidate (fault-tolerance / exactly-once tactics).

parked_architecture.name: Session State placement trio: Client Session State / Server Session State / Database Session State (PoEAA)
parked_architecture.named_in: Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (2002), ch. 17 (Session State patterns)
parked_architecture.rationale: Fails altitude upward: the three patterns are alternatives in a WHERE-does-session-state-live decision across tiers (client, app server, database) — a distribution/topology and statefulness decision about system structure, not an in-component mechanism. PoEAA itself frames them as a choice about server affinity, clustering, and failover. The in-process mechanisms they decompose into are already cataloged (abstract-session, security-session, serialized-lob, memento). Phase 3 candidates (state-placement / session-management architecture decisions).

excluded_notable.name: Allowed Lateness
excluded_notable.named_in: The Dataflow Model (PVLDB 2015); Apache Beam programming guide sec. 8.4 'Watermarks and late data' (verified live 2026-07-10)
excluded_notable.reason: Checked and rejected as a standalone element: a policy parameter (how long past the watermark window state is retained so late data can still fire late panes), not an independent mechanism — it exists only relative to windowing, watermark, and trigger. Folded: recorded as companion policy in the new stream-trigger entry; also fits as an aka/note on event-time-watermark.

excluded_notable.name: Value Holder (PoEAA lazy-load variant)
excluded_notable.reason: Already covered: 'value holder' is listed in the aka of the existing proxy entry (which absorbed Lazy Load/ghost/virtual proxy). No new element.

excluded_notable.name: Record Set (PoEAA)
excluded_notable.reason: Already in the index as record-set (data-representation). No new element.

excluded_notable.name: Pane accumulation modes (Discarding / Accumulating / Accumulating & Retracting)
excluded_notable.reason: Checked and rejected as standalone: refinement-relationship policy for successive trigger firings of the same window; meaningless without triggers. Folded into stream-trigger aka.

notes: Final-saturation gap hunt over two residual veins. (a) Streams: of the Dataflow Model's remaining named mechanisms only Trigger stands as a distinct element (output timing, vs windowing=grouping and watermark=completeness); allowed lateness and accumulation modes are dependent policies, folded and recorded. Chandy-Lamport/Flink-ABS snapshotting judged system-level and parked for Phase 3. (b) Fowler tail: PoEAA session-state trio parked upward (tier-placement decision); Value Holder and Record Set already covered by the index; the two established chapter-level DSL-book mechanisms absent from the index (Semantic Model, Expression Builder) were verified live on martinfowler.com/dslCatalog and added. Incidental observation while verifying the DSL catalog: most of its altitude-passing entries are already in the index under their canonical homes (parser-combinator, recursive-descent-parser, symbol-table, generation-gap, notification, method chaining under fluent-interface); Parser Generator is a tool category rather than an in-program mechanism and was not pursued. Yield 3 new / 2 parked / 4 rejected — consistent with saturation. No named_in corpus ids used: work_ids.tsv carries neither PoEAA, the Fowler DSL book, nor the Dataflow paper (only fowlerci/fowlerref for Fowler); all three are Phase 2 new-node candidates.
